title: Ankhorage Social
summary: Provides provider-neutral execution boundaries for publish, comment, and reaction actions.
purpose: Give independently released applications a typed social-action dispatch boundary without coupling workflows to OAuth, credential storage, or provider SDKs.
responsibilities: Publish typed commands, receipts, authorization ports, and provider ports for social actions.
Validate and dispatch publish, comment, and reaction commands through an explicitly selected provider capability.
Propagate opaque authorization references and caller-provided idempotency keys without persisting them.
boundaries: Does not own OAuth, credential storage, provider SDK authentication, or provider-specific payloads.
Does not execute Flow orchestration or persist action state, idempotency records, or receipts.
Does not require consumers to use unpublished sibling sources or an Ankhorage application.
audience: Application and workflow authors dispatching social actions through provider adapters.
Adapter authors implementing authorization and provider boundaries for social platforms.
useCases: Dispatch an authorized publish, comment, or reaction action to a matching provider adapter.
Reject malformed, unauthorized, mismatched, or unsupported actions before provider execution.

architecture.role: Provider-neutral social action library with explicit authorization and provider ports.
invariants: Social action dispatch remains independent from OAuth, credential storage, Flow execution, and provider SDKs.
Provider adapters own platform authentication, durable idempotency, and receipt persistence.
Consumers use the published package entrypoint and declared dependencies.

limitations: Provider capabilities, authorization decisions, idempotency guarantees, and receipts depend on caller-supplied adapters.
Only publish, comment, and reaction actions are represented by the current public API.
